> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **23** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0431b5bec7561c9720952a5cf02ca6c8918c1d51` — the merge of head `52e7cd7ccff36f221153d1dec165045f87bf5899` into base `35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0431b5bec7561c9720952a5cf02ca6c8918c1d51 && git checkout 0431b5bec7561c9720952a5cf02ca6c8918c1d51
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01 52e7cd7ccff36f221153d1dec165045f87bf5899 && git checkout -B drift-repro 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01 && git merge --no-ff 52e7cd7ccff36f221153d1dec165045f87bf5899

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `52e7cd7ccff36f221153d1dec165045f87bf5899`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-link-action.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-invitation.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-delivery-outcome.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/invitation-delivery-copy.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts, packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts, ui/packages/core/src/utils/predicate-fields.ts, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/objectGridQueryInputs.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/invitation-screens-copy.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.inviteOutcome-27797.test.tsx, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the changeset `.changeset/28384-expired-invitation-link.md` is a prose face, read for its declaration lines and for security discipline, not reviewed)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and on the changeset). No path under `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path is in the committed tree (`record-recognisers.mjs --paths` on the five files decides no face by path and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line), so the narrowing face is the only face owed and its floor is every non-prose path of the diff, listed first in `Scope:`. Inputs read: card #28384 and triage comment 6541933328, the seat's order for #28384, the dev report comment 6553647203, the PR body and its one commit, the head's check runs through the REST API. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note is owed under ③.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Which calls move from answered to refused.** Exactly one: the platform action door `sys_invitation.copy_invitation_link`, for a caller who already passes every earlier gate (not cloud-managed, a named record, a signed-in caller, invite reach in the invitation's organization, `status == 'pending'`), on a row whose `expires_at` is not strictly in the future. Before this head that call answered `200 { acceptUrl }`; at this head it answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Correct: that is the whole narrowing the card asks for, and nothing else in the handler's accept set moves. The handler's `fields` read gains `expires_at` and nothing else; the four earlier refusals keep their status, code and sentence; the pre-expiry pending row keeps its answer (pinned for a `Date`, ISO text and epoch-milliseconds value). Judged correct.
2. **Boundary at `expires_at == now`.** `isBeforeExpiry` answers `ms > Date.now()`, so a row whose expiry equals the instant of the call is read as expired and refused; the `visible` predicate's `datetime(record.expires_at) > now()` hides it at the same instant. Handler and courtesy agree on the closed boundary, and for a bearer credential the closed side is the right one: the link is offered only while it still has a future. Judged correct.
3. **Null, absent or unreadable `expires_at`.** The field is `required: true` on `sys_invitation`, so a null is a row the vendor never wrote; the handler reads it as expired (`isBeforeExpiry` answers `false` for anything that is not a `Date`, string or number, and for a value whose `getTime()` is not finite) and `visible` hides it (`has(record.expires_at) && record.expires_at != null` fails). Fail-closed on both faces, and the test pins both the handler case (`'not a date'`) and the predicate cases (key absent, key null). Judged correct. One caveat in ④ below on the vendor claim the docblock makes.
4. **Gate order.** The new gate is the sixth, after the pending gate, in the order the docblock lists (cloud-managed, record, caller, reach, pending, not expired). A caller outside invite reach on an expired row still answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` and learns nothing about the row, pinned by the new reach-before-expiry test. Judged correct.
5. **Code and wording family.** `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, the same status and code as the status gate, and the same sentence frame as the status gate's first sentence (`..., so its link no longer lets anyone join.`), with a second sentence naming the remedy. The order proposed `Resend it to start its expiry over.`; the dev wrote `Resend the invitation to give the person a link that works.` The dev's wording is the correct one: measured on the installed vendor, a resend on an expired pending row issues a new invitation rather than renewing the row, so the order's sentence would have promised something the system does not do. Judged correct, and an improvement on the order.
6. **The `visible` expression.** `features.cloudManaged != true && has(record.status) && record.status == 'pending' && has(record.expires_at) && record.expires_at != null && datetime(record.expires_at) > now()`. The ordering comparison carries the full conjunction `has(record.x) && record.x != null` that `materializeDeclaredFields` (`packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts`) prescribes for the sparse action face before any ordering use, which is one half more than the equality-only `status` operand needs, and the comment on the declaration says exactly why. The comparison's form, `datetime(record.FIELD)` against a temporal, is the form the repo already uses on a declared predicate (`sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`: `datetime(record.valid_until) <= datetime(record.valid_from)`); `datetime(dyn)` resolves through `toDate`, which accepts a `Date`, ISO text or epoch number, so the list row's ISO text and a detail read both evaluate; `now()` is the stdlib temporal bound to the evaluation's `ctx.now ?? new Date()`, and the engine's temporal equality rewrite does not touch an ordering. Judged correct.
7. **Every list view that offers the action projects `expires_at`.** `pending` projects it as a column. `all_invitations` does not, and the pending rows it lists are the ones the action reaches; it is covered because the grid harvests every `record.FIELD` an action `visible` names into `$select` (`listViewPredicates` pushes `rowActionDefs[].visible`, `collectPredicateFieldRefs` reads `record.expires_at` out of the `datetime(...)` call by its `\b(record|data)\.name` match, and `isProjectableField` admits it as a declared field). `accepted` and `expired` never show a pending row. The predicate test pins the absent-key case as `false`, so a surface that neither projects nor harvests hides the action rather than offering it. Judged correct; see ③ for the one surface outside this repo.
8. **`visible` is courtesy, the handler is the enforcement.** The dev's ablation disabled the handler gate alone with `visible` at head and the two handler cases went red; the handler re-reads the row under the system context and never trusts the projected record. Read from the report, not re-run. Judged correct.
9. **Generated translation files.** None of the four `*.objects.generated.ts` bundles is in the diff. The bundle carries the action's `label` and `resultDialog` only, never its `visible`; the handler's refusal sentences are not bundled (the existing status-gate sentence is not either). Nothing was hand-edited and nothing needed regenerating. Judged correct.
10. **Served shape of the object definition.** No field, key, option, list view or action is added, removed or renamed on `sys_invitation`; one action's `visible` value changes. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true. Judged correct.
11. **First-party callers assuming the old answer.** None found. The console runs the action through the generic action runtime and shows whatever the door answers; `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/manage/InviteMemberDialog.tsx` composes its link from invite-member's own answer, not from this action; `docs/adr/0011-actions-as-ai-tools.md` only names the action; no `skills/**`, `packages/client` or `content/docs` consumer reads `acceptUrl` from this door. The UI fixture `ObjectView.inviteOutcome-27797.test.tsx` carries its own status-only copy of the predicate and mocks the door at 200, so it asserts nothing about an expired row; it does not fall out of step with this change.
12. **Security discipline.** PR body, the one commit message, the changeset, the handler docblock, the declaration comment and the test names all stay on the public story (an expired invitation's link is no longer offered or answered; resend is the remedy). None describes a mechanism for using a stale link. Nothing logs the link. Judged clean.
13. **Resend.** The ruling says `apply the same check to resend`; the card's own Expected line reads `the same rule applies to resend if it shares the check`. The dev measured that `resend_invitation` does not share the check (its `visible` is the lowered feature and reach gates only, no status operand), left it offered on an expired row and added no expiry refusal, and says so in the PR body and in the changeset's Unchanged bullet. That reading is sound: nothing moves a row to `expired`, so a resend that refused on expiry would remove the only way an admin can give the invitee a working link, which is the opposite of the card's purpose; and the PR pins that a resend on an expired row answers 200 and that the link of the invitation it answers is then copyable. Judged correct.

### ② Semver level

The changeset grades `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` both `patch`, declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: none`, and carries a `**BREAKING**` banner. That is the shape the gates require: under `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` a `none` must grade every entry it introduces `patch` and may not move an `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline, and no `packages/spec/**` file (so no `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` shard) is in the diff; `narrowed` is not owed, because the protocol an author writes against does not change, only a platform action's own predicate value. Both packages publish (neither manifest is private), so a changeset, not `skip-changeset`, is right under `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`, and the frontmatter is not empty. The `Clause-②` value is the correct one: `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads `no (narrowing)` as "NOT a widening, but breaking", and `yes (narrowing)` as a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; this diff widens none, and `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` says the same ("a card that only NARROWS one is `Clause-②: no`"). The order expected `yes (narrowing)`; the dev measured and corrected it, and says so under Acceptance notes. The `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition beside a BREAKING banner is a pairing the ADR-0087 gate's own docblock names as an author's entitlement, and `Check Changeset` and the three `Lint` jobs that run the two gates are green on this head. Level and declaration agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev raised no `open_questions`. One `out_of_scope_findings` entry, carrier none, noted in the PR and not filed: on the installed vendor a resend of an expired pending invitation issues a new invitation and leaves the expired row reading `pending`, so Resend's confirmation sentence (`Its expiry date starts over.`) is not what happens there and the Pending list then shows two rows for one person. This review agrees it is outside the card and does not block; it is a real defect in the remedy path this PR points admins at, so the seat should file it as its own card rather than leave it as a note in a PR body. Not a must-fix here.
- The card says cloud's team page uses the framework's action as-is (objectstack-ai/cloud PR 3429). That repository is not readable from this session. If that page evaluates the action's `visible` over a row projection of its own without `expires_at`, the new `has(record.expires_at)` operand hides the action there, fail-closed; that is the right direction for a credential and the handler is unaffected, but the cloud lane should confirm the page projects `expires_at` or harvests predicate operands as the console grid does. Flag for the seat to relay; not a must-fix in this repository.
- The vendor's source (better-auth 1.7.12, pinned in `pnpm-lock.yaml`) could not be opened from this session (no installed `node_modules`, registry egress refused). The handler docblock's statements about the vendor (its accept route refuses past `expires_at`; an unreadable value reads as expired) rest on the dev's measurements in the plugin-auth harness over the installed vendor, which the new tests pin at the behaviour level (an expired row is refused by this handler; a pre-expiry row answers for three value shapes). The handler's own correctness does not depend on the vendor claim.
- At review time every `Lint`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` check run is green; the eight `Test Core` shards and `Type Check · workspace` are still in progress. The landing pre-check (all checks green on the landing head) is the seat's read before the queue, not this record's.
- The commit subject reads `fix(plugin-auth):` while the PR title reads `fix(plugin-auth)!:`; the squash title is what lands and `check-commit-card-trailers` is green, so nothing is owed. Noted only.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the spec on `main`: no declared capability is taken away from a consumer. `copy_invitation_link` was declared, and documented in its own `resultDialog`, as a link that stops working once the invitation expires; before this head the action handed over a link that the accept route would already refuse, so the published promise and the served behaviour disagreed, and this head makes the action's own refusal real rather than removing anything an author or a consumer could rely on. The two halves land in the right places for a bearer credential: the handler, which runs system-elevated at the action door and re-reads the row, carries the enforcement, and the declaration's predicate follows it as courtesy, exactly the division the handler's docblock has stated since the action was added. The refusal is a 409 in the status gate's family, so a client that already handles the non-pending refusal handles this one with no new branch. Reading missing or unreadable expiry as expired is fail-closed in the direction the four-axis rule prefers (a strict door over a lenient consumer), and the test pins it so an AI-written row or driver cannot widen it silently. The remedy sentence tells the admin the one thing that works and does not promise a renewal the vendor does not perform, which is why the dev's wording is preferred over the order's. The `visible` expression is the published form for this face (the full guard conjunction, `datetime()` on the operand, `now()` from the stdlib), so it neither faults on the sparse row nor offers the action when the key is absent, and the grid's predicate harvest keeps the `all_invitations` view honest without a new column. Leaving `resend_invitation` ungated is the design the ruling's purpose requires: the ruling wants no dead link offered, and the resend is how a live one is obtained. The changes hold against the code they cite (`materializeDeclaredFields`, `collectPredicateFieldRefs`, the stdlib temporal functions) and against the card's acceptance scenario (a pending row past `expires_at` is hidden and refused, pre-expiry and non-pending rows keep their answers, resend is unchanged). No must-fix.
